newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Jan layoffs up 16.5 versus Dec -- Challenger.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Jan layoffs up 16.5 versus Dec -- Challenger.

text.p: January layoffs totaled 43,595, up 16.5 percent over December, but down 55 percent from the total for January 1996, according to a report by Challenger, Gray & Christmas Inc.
Reflecting a weaker-than-expected holiday sales season, job layoffs in the retail sector "accounted for more than one out of every five announced cuts in January," the report said.
And in the past four months, over 26,000 retail layoffs have been announced, it said.
January job cuts were the second largest in the past six months, and the third largest monthly drop since January 1996, "when AT&T's announcement boosted the monthly total," the report said.

Among the retailers who led in announced layoffs last month were: McCrory Corp, with 3,500 job cuts; Service Merchandise and Ernst Home Centers Inc, tied at 1,500 each; and Petrie Inc, with 1,000 job cuts, according to a monthly Challenger Employment Report released on Thursday.

"Heavy job cuts in retail were not completely unexpected, especially after a holiday season that was very dissapointing to some retailers," said John Challenger, first executive vice president of the outplacement firm.
He said poor cash register sales have induced many companies to adjust the size of their payrolls or close stores to compensate for the losses.
"Despite the relatively high January job-cut figure, the economy remains strong and it is still a job hunter's paradise for many job seekers," he said.
